papers.title: Functional 3D Neural Mini‐Tissues from Printed Gel‐Based Bioink and Human Neural Stem Cells
papers.abstract: Direct-write printing of stem cells within biomaterials presents an opportunity to engineer tissue for in vitro modeling and regenerative medicine. Here, a first example of constructing neural tissue by printing human neural stem cells that are differentiated in situ to functional neurons and supporting neuroglia is reported. The supporting biomaterial incorporates a novel clinically relevant polysaccharide-based bioink comprising alginate, carboxymethyl-chitosan, and agarose. The printed bioink rapidly gels by stable cross-linking to form a porous 3D scaffold encapsulating stem cells for in situ expansion and differentiation. Differentiated neurons form synaptic contacts, establish networks, are spontaneously active, show a bicuculline-induced increased calcium response, and are predominantly gamma-aminobutyric acid expressing. The 3D tissues will facilitate investigation of human neural development, function, and disease, and may be adaptable for engineering other 3D tissues from different stem cell types.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及任何人工智能方法，与AI生物打印方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper presents a bioprinting method for neural tissue but contains no AI/ML integration, no autonomous decision-making, and no computational workflow optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 构建功能性3D神经组织用于体外建模和再生医学。
summary_zh.method: 使用直接书写打印技术将人神经干细胞封装在多糖基生物墨水中进行原位分化。
summary_zh.result: 分化出的神经元形成突触连接和网络，具有自发活性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过钙成像和免疫染色验证神经元功能。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate functional 3D neural tissues for in vitro modeling and regenerative medicine applications.
summary_en.method: Human neural stem cells were printed within a polysaccharide-based bioink (alginate, carboxymethyl-chitosan, agarose) and differentiated in situ.
summary_en.result: Differentiated neurons formed synaptic contacts, established networks, and exhibited spontaneous calcium activity.
summary_en.validation: Functional validation was performed via calcium imaging and immunostaining for neural markers.
